MANGLO SELLER GUIDES

JPG, PNG or WebP: which format should you choose?

The best image format depends on the image and where you plan to use it. A photograph, a transparent logo and a screenshot with small lettering have different needs. Here is a practical way to choose.

JPG: a familiar choice for photos

JPG is widely supported and is usually a practical option for product photography. It uses lossy compression: a lower quality setting reduces file size by discarding more information. It does not support transparency. Manglo fills transparent areas with white when exporting JPG.

PNG: transparency and crisp graphics

PNG supports transparency and lossless compression. It is useful for logos, interface screenshots and graphics with flat colors or sharp edges. A detailed photo exported as PNG can be much larger than a JPG. Moving the quality slider does not make PNG lossy.

WebP: flexible, efficient delivery

WebP supports transparency and can provide smaller files for many images. It is a useful choice for modern websites, but confirm that your listing platform, editor or upload form accepts it before converting a whole catalog.

SituationStarting choice
Product photo for broad compatibilityJPG
Transparent logo or sharp graphicPNG
Website photo where WebP is supportedWebP

Compare using the same dimensions

Export the same image at the same pixel size in two formats. Compare file size and visible detail, particularly around edges, gradients and text. A format name alone does not tell you which result will be smaller or clearer.

Keep the source

Repeatedly opening and saving a lossy image can introduce additional artifacts. Keep the original and create each export from that source. Manglo is intended for still images; animated inputs are exported as one frame, and most metadata is removed.
